messages:
Maria G: Heads-up: marketing will run a week-long holiday promo Dec 20-27. Product expects ~2x peak sessions in NA-east (east1). Can we run an admit-curve + GPU-hour forecast?
Sam K: Do we have baseline numbers to plug in? p95/p99 targets?
Maria G: Baseline concurrent sessions at peak ~750. SLA: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms. Current east1 fleet: 48 A100 equiv GPUs. Our measured slot density for this workload = ~24 concurrent sessions/GPU to keep p99<=300ms.
Kai L: Ok. If peak doubles to 1500 concurrent sessions then naive capacity math: required_gpus = ceil(1500 / 24) = 63.
Sam K: Can you paste the quick calc?
Maria G: Sure:
```python
import math
peak = 1500
slots_per_gpu = 24
required = math.ceil(peak/slots_per_gpu)
gpu_hours_per_day = required * 24
print(required, gpu_hours_per_day)  # 63, 1512
```
Josh P: So 63 GPUs * 24h = 1512 GPU-hours/day. At our list burn of ~$3.20 / GPU-hour ~= $4.84k/day. Rough but useful for finance.
Kai L: We have mitigations:
- quantize to int8 for this model -> raises slots/GPU to ~34 (measured in perf lab)
- enable prefix + KV caching for repeat prompts -> reduces average work by ~12%
- route overflow to us-central fallback region (higher RTT but spare capacity)
Sam K: If quantize -> required = ceil(1500/34) = 45 GPUs -> 1080 GPU-hours/day -> cost ~ $3.45k/day.
Maria G: Tradeoffs: int8 increases small regression risk. We should pair quantize with eval harness for the top-10 prompt families.
Kai L: Also note: east1 peering has been showing transient egress congestion during 16:00-18:00 UTC historically (adds ~40ms tail). That bit pushes p99 above budget even if GPU count is OK. We should add a network safety margin.
Josh P: Proposal: soft admission cap at 1200 concurrent sessions in east1, overflow routed to us-central. That gives p99 cushion and prevents tail blowouts.
Maria G: Agreed. With soft cap 1200 -> required_gpus = ceil(1200/24)=50 GPUs -> 1200 GPU-hours/day.
```bash
# quick numbers
peak=1200
slots=24
echo $(( (peak + slots -1) / slots ))  # 50
```
infra-bot: Autoscaler: tentative plan queued: target_capacity=70 GPUs for east1 (prewarm + headroom), prewarm_window=2h before 50% expected peak, fallback_route=us-central. See runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/east1-holiday-prep
Sam K: Why 70 and not 63/50? headroom for degraded nodes and network noise?
Kai L: Yes — pick conservative: 63 active compute GPUs + ~10% spare for node churn, realtime failover and canary (63 * 1.1 ≈ 69.3). We also want room for bursts.
Maria G: Canary plan: Dec 18 at 16:00 UTC -> spin an extra 12 GPUs for 2h, run synthetic traces targeting p99 and quantized model evals. If metrics look good, enable full prewarm on Dec 20.
Josh P: Action items:
- Kai: run quantize eval suite for top-10 prompts by EOD Friday (include quality deltas)
- Sam: draft admit rule: soft_cap=1200, hard_cap=1500 -> overflow to us-central; add circuit-breaker at 1600 to reject lower-priority traffic
- Maria: coordinate with marketing on exact promo windows so we can tighten windows and reduce prepaid hours
- infra-bot: please schedule autoscaler change and post a follow-up thread with exact rollback steps
Maria G: thanks all :thumbsup: Let's reconvene Monday if any test shows regression.
infra-bot: Note: I'm posting an audit event when the autoscaler plan is promoted to prod.
